newsitem.title: FRANCE: Michelin says car taxes high, wary of EMU.
newsitem.headline: Michelin says car taxes high, wary of EMU.

text.p: Francois Michelin, the biggest shareholder of the Michelin tyre company, said the trouble with Europe's car industry was that costs were too high and governments taxed cars too much.

In a brief interview with Reuters at the Paris car show, he also sounded wary about European Monetary Union. "I'm not sure a single currency will give the men and women of Europe the necessary flexibility to develop," he said.
He also said European currencies needed to reach the right levels ahead of the move to a single currency but declined to say which currencies he had in mind.
Taking the image of a canal, Michelin said: "You can't open the locks until the water levels are even. The leader of Europe would have to be a lock-keeper, and then it would work better."
The Michelin patriarch said he was impressed by the models on display at the car show but said the industry was struggling through a difficult time.

"Governments aren't doing what they should so that cars can circulate freely, they tax them much too much, and they don't build the necessary infrastructure," he said. "If in the industry, we built systems as dangerous as some two- and three-lane roads we'd go to prison," he added.
Michelin said cost structures in the European car industry were so high that it faced "enormous difficulties" relative to U.S., Japanese, Korean and eventually Chinese rivals.
